title: CIC agent tricks Schauberger into signing his work over; IP ends up at Brookhaven
place_text: Europe; Brookhaven National Lab, Long Island

tellings.quote: After the war ended, another Army CIC agent, Neil Gershimer, tricked Shawberger into signing all of his work over to the United States.

plain: After the Second World War, an agent of the Army's Counter Intelligence Corps named Neil Gershimer is said to have tricked a man named Victor Shawberger into signing all of his work over to the United States, and that work is said to have ended up at Brookhaven, a government research lab on Long Island. Michels tells this himself without naming a source, as part of a story about the US quietly gathering unusual wartime science.
